name: harbor-voices-naturalistic-200
origin: Project-authored fictional naturalistic dialogue; Codex author and label reviewer; not independent human gold or a held-out sample.

turns.text: I'm Asha Patel. I'm coordinating Harbor Voices, an oral-history project about our neighborhood's old waterfront. I need help keeping the practical details straight.
Let's start with the people and the project constraints. What is your role?
My job title is community archivist. The interviews are a side project at the library, rather than a new department.
That gives us a useful scope. Who approves decisions for your work?
Priya Nair is my manager. Morgan helps with the interviews, but Morgan doesn't manage me.
Understood. Where will you usually be working?
I live in Boston, and my work timezone is America/New_York. Please keep the timezone in invitations even when everyone seems local.
Explicit timezones will help with guests who travel. What tools are already in place?
We use PostgreSQL for the catalog. That's an existing choice from the library, not a statement that it's my favorite database.
I'll treat that as current database use. How are you preparing the catalog data?
I write the import scripts in Python. Neovim is my editor, and fish is my interactive shell.
Those are three separate tool choices. How do you track project work?
We track issues in Linear. Interview notes live in Obsidian, though the final catalog records go into the database.
We can keep task links and notes separate from catalog records. Is there an initial budget?
My monthly transcription budget is 100 dollars. That's the approved ceiling for now; I haven't asked for an increase yet.
I'll use that ceiling when comparing transcription options. Are there meeting constraints?
Wednesday is my meeting-free day. I need a long block for cleaning the old spreadsheets.
Then Wednesday should stay clear of interview planning calls. Anything needed for the other calls?
I need captions enabled on video calls. Please make that part of our normal setup, not something I have to request every time.
I'll include captions in the call setup notes. We can build the interview checklist next.
I've booked the first interview for April 10 with Lena Ortiz. She's bringing photographs from her family's shop.
That gives the first session a clear focus. Where is it happening?
The first interview is in the library's Cedar Room. I reserved it from 2 to 4 pm.
Two hours should include setup and packing time. What recording equipment is available?
I borrowed a Zoom H5 recorder from the media desk yesterday. I own the headphones, but the recorder has to go back after the session.
I'll distinguish the loan from your own equipment. Have you checked the room's sound?
I tested the Cedar Room this morning. The ventilation hum is audible near the door, so I want the table by the window.
The seating plan can reflect that test. How will you handle the photographs?
I'll scan the photographs after the interview, if Lena agrees. I haven't received permission to scan them yet.
The checklist should make scanning conditional on consent. What should we record before starting audio?
Our consent form is version 3. The library requires the participant's signature before recording begins.
I'll put the consent check ahead of the recorder check. Do you have the form ready?
Yes, I printed two copies. One is for Lena and one is for our locked project folder.
That covers both copies. What do you want to learn in this first interview?
My main question for Lena is how the waterfront businesses changed when the ferry terminal moved. I don't want to turn it into a general family biography.
We can use the terminal move as the central thread and let family details support it.
Could you suggest three open questions that don't assume the move was bad for every shop?
You could ask what changed, which changes were surprising, and how different businesses responded. Each leaves room for mixed experiences.
Those work. I'll bring a large-print copy of the prompts because Lena asked for one.
I'll add the large-print prompts to the packing list.
Priya approved the budget increase today. The monthly transcription ceiling is now 150 dollars, replacing the old 100-dollar limit.
I'll use the updated ceiling for future planning.
We also moved the first interview to April 13. Lena has a family commitment on the 10th; the person and room are unchanged.
The date changed while the interview's other details stayed stable.
The reservation on April 13 is still 2 to 4 pm in Cedar Room. I confirmed it with the front desk.
I'll keep that confirmation with the interview details.
I'm considering buying a second recorder, but I haven't chosen a model or committed to spending the money.
We can leave that as an open equipment question rather than a purchase.
For editing audio I use Audacity. Please don't put that under databases just because we mentioned PostgreSQL earlier.
Audio editing and catalog storage will remain separate tool records.
I prefer plain-text checklists over a new project-management app. Linear is enough for the team's tasks.
I can keep the working checklist in plain text.
The team has four volunteers, including Morgan. I coordinate their schedules, but they're not my employees.
I'll describe them as volunteers and keep scheduling separate from employment relationships.
Morgan handles recording setup, and Jules checks the scanned images. I review catalog metadata before it goes public.
That gives the handoff clear responsibilities.
Could we use one shared spreadsheet as a temporary intake list? I'm asking about the workflow, not saying we've adopted it.
A temporary intake sheet could work if it links to source files and has a clear owner. It would still need a decision from your team.
Let's leave intake as it is until after the first interview. I don't want to change three things in the same week.
We'll revisit intake after that session, when you have a concrete example to work from.
The interview with Lena is finished. We recorded 74 minutes of audio in Cedar Room on April 13.
That gives us a completed session to process. How did the equipment perform?
The borrowed recorder worked well. I returned the Zoom H5 to the media desk this afternoon.
I'll mark the loan as returned rather than owned equipment.
Lena signed the recording form, but she asked us to keep one story off the public website until she reviews the transcript.
The public release needs to wait for that review. Did she agree to scanning the photographs?
Yes, she gave written permission to scan eight photographs. We scanned all eight after the interview.
I'll separate permission from the completed scanning work.
I saved the originals as TIFF files. The JPEG copies are only for browsing, and shouldn't replace the originals.
The archive and browsing copies will have separate roles.
We caught a spelling mistake in Lena's surname on the intake sheet. It's Ortiz, with a z; the interview recording itself is fine.
The spelling correction belongs in the intake metadata.
I haven't finished the transcript. The automatic draft confuses the old shop names, so I'm checking them against the photographs.
The draft should remain marked as unreviewed while you check those names.
My review deadline for that draft is April 18. I promised to send Lena a readable copy before asking about publication.
I'll keep the review deadline tied to Lena's transcript.
The noise cleanup can wait. The words and names matter more than making the recording sound polished.
We'll prioritize transcript accuracy before audio cleanup.
Can you turn those next steps into a short checklist?
Review shop names, check the surname in metadata, send the readable transcript by April 18, and hold the restricted story until Lena responds.
Quick correction for our meeting schedule: Monday is now my meeting-free day, not Wednesday. The library moved my public desk shift.
I'll update the recurring meeting constraint to Monday.
Wednesday afternoons are available for project calls now. Please don't infer that I work every Wednesday evening as well.
I'll keep afternoon availability separate from evening work.
The volunteer handoff is on Saturday. It used to happen on Friday, but the media desk no longer opens late that day.
Saturday will be the recurring handoff day.
My emergency contact is Eli Patel. Morgan is a colleague, and should not be listed as my emergency contact.
I'll keep Eli as the contact and distinguish Morgan's project role.
For the volunteer lunch, remember that I have a peanut allergy. It isn't simply a food preference.
I'll retain that as an allergy for planning the lunch.
I usually bring vegetarian food, but I haven't said that every volunteer is vegetarian.
Your usual food choice won't be applied to the whole group.
We have two new volunteers, so there are six in total now. Morgan is still handling recording setup.
I'll update the total from four to six.
Could you suggest a ten-minute introduction for the new volunteers? They need to understand consent before they touch equipment.
Start with why consent matters, walk through the form, and demonstrate where recording starts and stops. Then let them ask about a concrete scenario.
That order makes sense. I've scheduled the introduction for Saturday at 10 am, just before handoff.
I'll keep the introduction time attached to Saturday's session.
What if we eventually ran a second project in another neighborhood? It's only a possibility, so don't add another active project yet.
We can leave expansion as an idea for a later review.
Lena returned her transcript edits yesterday. She approved the corrected shop names, but the restricted story still needs another conversation.
The name review is complete, while the release restriction remains open.
I finished the transcript review on April 18 as planned. The current transcript status is reviewed, with one passage held from publication.
I'll keep those as separate review and release states.
Our next interview is with Omar Haddad on April 24. He worked at the ferry terminal for thirty years.
We can prepare questions about the terminal from his perspective.
Omar prefers a phone interview. I will call him from the library; he isn't coming to Cedar Room.
The session format is phone, so the room setup can stay minimal.
I want to ask about his own work first, then the terminal move. I don't know whether he agrees with Lena's account.
The prompts should leave space for a different account.
We added a field called rights_status to the catalog. Its values are pending, cleared, and restricted.
That should make publication readiness explicit.
I use Python for imports and SQL for catalog queries. Neither statement means I've switched my preferred programming language.
I'll keep those usage roles separate from preference.
For my own scripts, Python is still my primary language. The SQL work is part of the catalog maintenance.
The primary-language fact stays Python.
Can you help me write a query that lists records with pending rights, without changing any records?
A read-only query can select records whose rights_status equals pending. We should confirm the table name before making it executable.
The table is interviews. I only want interview_id, participant_name, and rights_status in that export.
That gives us the table and the three columns needed for the export.
The phone interview with Omar happened on April 24 and lasted 51 minutes. We covered his terminal job and the ferry schedule changes.
I'll record it as a completed interview with those topics.
I had a follow-up question about a route number, so I emailed him. He hasn't replied yet.
That route number should remain unresolved rather than guessed.
Morgan noticed that one audio filename used April 23 by mistake. The interview was April 24; please keep that correction attached to Omar's recording.
I'll use April 24 for Omar's recording and note the filename correction.
I'm considering an exhibition in June, but we don't have approval or a venue. For now it's an idea, not a scheduled event.
We'll keep June exhibition planning tentative.
We do have a confirmed review meeting on May 2 with Priya. That's about the archive, not an exhibition launch.
The May 2 event is an archive review meeting.
I made a sample page using three photographs, all from the cleared set. The restricted story isn't on it.
The sample can demonstrate the layout while respecting the release status.
I'd like the page to use a readable serif typeface. I haven't picked a particular font yet.
We can compare a few readable serif options without marking one as selected.
The first sample had tiny captions. I increased the caption size after Jules tried it on a small laptop.
That feedback should guide the next sample as well.
Can you propose a short usability check for the page?
Ask someone to find a photograph's date, identify who is speaking, and locate the rights note. Watch where they hesitate before changing the layout.
I'll try that with two volunteers on Wednesday afternoon. Please keep Monday free as we agreed.
The usability check can use Wednesday afternoon while Monday remains meeting-free.
The usability check is done. Both volunteers found the photo dates, but neither noticed the rights note without a hint.
The rights note needs a more visible position.
We moved the rights note directly below the title. I don't want to hide it in a hover tooltip.
I'll keep the visible placement as the current design decision.
I bought an external SSD for project backups on April 28. It cost 90 dollars, which came from the equipment budget rather than transcription.
I'll keep the equipment purchase separate from the monthly transcription ceiling.
The transcription ceiling is still 150 dollars per month. The SSD purchase didn't reduce it to 60.
The monthly transcription limit remains 150 dollars.
I run a backup every Thursday afternoon. The SSD is stored in the locked cabinet after each backup.
That gives the backup routine both a schedule and a storage location.
We tested restoring one interview yesterday. The audio and transcript both opened correctly from the backup.
I'll record the successful restore test rather than assume all future backups are valid.
Priya asked for a one-page review brief. It should cover interviews, permissions, budget, and the next two weeks of work.
Those four topics can form a compact brief.
I don't want to include a made-up completion percentage. We have two completed interviews and several unfinished tasks; those counts are clearer.
We can report the completed interview count and list the open tasks.
Could you draft the outline without inventing outcomes from the May 2 review?
Yes: completed interviews, current release restrictions, actual spending and budget ceilings, open follow-ups, and proposed next steps. Review outcomes stay blank until the meeting occurs.
That's the right scope. I'll finish the brief tomorrow morning before sending it to Priya.
The brief remains a planned task until you've finished and sent it.
We held the archive review on May 2. Priya approved continuing Harbor Voices for another month, but didn't approve an exhibition.
I'll distinguish the project extension from the exhibition idea.
The manager relationship hasn't changed: Priya Nair is still my manager. Morgan ran part of the meeting because I was presenting the sample page.
Running part of a meeting doesn't change who manages you.
Lena has now cleared the previously restricted story for publication. I saved her written approval with the interview record.
That changes the release condition for her story.
Omar replied with the route number too. His answer was route 17, not route 70 as the automatic transcript guessed.
I'll preserve route 17 as the corrected value and keep it tied to his follow-up.
We corrected the transcript and marked Omar's follow-up resolved. The raw recording wasn't edited to match the text.
The corrected transcript and unchanged recording can remain separate source artifacts.
The public catalog preview is planned for May 16. That's a preview of cleared material, not the June exhibition we discussed.
I'll keep the preview and exhibition as different events.
I prefer PostgreSQL to MongoDB for this catalog now that I've worked with both. That is an actual preference, unlike my earlier statement about what the library already used.
I'll record that explicit preference separately from database use.
We still use PostgreSQL. Please don't replace that with MongoDB just because it appeared in the comparison.
The current database-use fact stays PostgreSQL.
I have a new volunteer named Theo helping with the preview. With Theo, the total is seven volunteers.
I'll update the volunteer total to seven.
Can you list the remaining launch tasks without treating every idea we've discussed as a commitment?
The remaining list can focus on cleared catalog records, the preview page, rights notes and final checks. The unapproved exhibition and possible second project stay outside it.
The catalog preview moved from May 16 to May 19. We need the extra time for accessibility checks, and Priya agreed to the change.
I'll update the preview date while preserving why it moved.
The captions requirement still applies to our video calls. For the catalog page itself, we're checking image descriptions and keyboard navigation.
Those are separate accessibility needs for calls and the page.
Jules found two images with missing descriptions. I wrote descriptions for both this morning, but we still need someone else to review them.
I'll mark the descriptions as drafted and awaiting review.
We aren't changing the TIFF originals. The description updates belong in catalog metadata and the browsing page.
I'll keep descriptive metadata separate from the original image files.
The Saturday volunteer handoff is staying put. The date change for the preview doesn't move that recurring handoff to Tuesday.
The recurring handoff remains Saturday.
My emergency contact is still Eli Patel. Alex Chen is the equipment vendor's contact, so please don't merge those two people.
I'll retain Eli as your emergency contact and keep the vendor contact separate.
I listened to a lot of jazz while editing last week. That doesn't mean I want a permanent favorite-genre entry; my listening changes with the task.
I'll treat that as recent listening context rather than a lasting preference.
Could you summarize the current dates, budget and contacts for the next person helping me? Please include the corrections, not just the first values you saw.
The summary should use the latest confirmed values and keep unresolved items clearly marked. I can organize it as a short handoff note.
One last detail for that note: the project email is harbor-voices@example.org. Use that address for participant scheduling, not my personal inbox.
I'll use the project address in the scheduling handoff.
Thanks. After the preview, I want to review which notes were actually useful before we add more automation. We can leave exhibition planning for another conversation.
That gives the next review a practical focus: keep useful notes, inspect mistakes and decide what automation is justified.
